nutritionPage.title: Our Nutritional Philosophy
nutritionPage.subtitle: How NutriApp thinks about food, balance, and long-term health
nutritionPage.intro: NutriApp isn't about perfection. It's about awareness. The science behind this app draws from decades of nutritional research to give you a framework that is both practical and sustainable — without obsession or guilt.

section1.title: Real food first
section1.body: The most consistent finding in nutritional science is simple: diets built around minimally processed whole foods — vegetables, legumes, whole grains, fish, nuts, and fruit — are associated with lower rates of chronic disease, better energy, and healthier body weight. This holds across cultures, climates, and eating styles. NutriApp is built around this principle. We don't prescribe a single diet, but all our feedback is grounded in favouring real food over ultra-processed alternatives.

section2.title: The problem with ultra-processed foods
section2.body: Ultra-processed foods (UPFs) — think packaged snacks, reconstituted meat products, sweetened beverages, and most fast food — are engineered to be hyper-palatable, cheap to produce, and easy to overconsume. Research consistently links high UPF intake to obesity, type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and even depression. The issue isn't just calories: it's the combination of refined ingredients, additives, and the displacement of nutritious whole foods. When NutriApp flags a product's processing level, it's drawing on this evidence base — not moralising, but informing.
section2.imageCaption: Whole foods vs. ultra-processed: the difference goes beyond calories

section3.title: Calories: useful but incomplete
section3.body: Calories matter — but they are not the whole story. 500 kcal of lentils and vegetables affects your body very differently than 500 kcal of white bread and margarine. Protein and fibre promote satiety. Refined carbohydrates spike blood sugar. Fat composition matters. NutriApp tracks calories because they provide a useful reference point, but we also track protein, fibre, and macronutrient balance so you can see the full picture. The goal is not to eat less — it is to eat better.
section3.imageCaption: Calorie counts can be equal; nutritional quality rarely is

section4.title: Protein: the underrated anchor
section4.body: Adequate protein is one of the most consistent levers for body composition, satiety, and metabolic health. Most adults benefit from 1.2–2.0 g of protein per kg of body weight per day, yet many people fall well short of this without realising it. Good sources include eggs, fish, poultry, legumes, dairy, and tofu. NutriApp highlights your daily protein intake precisely because it is easy to overlook — and because getting it right makes everything else easier.

section5.title: Healthy balance over rigid rules
section5.body: No single food is inherently good or bad. Chronic patterns matter far more than individual meals. A pizza on Friday doesn't undo a week of thoughtful eating. NutriApp is designed to help you see those patterns over time — not to punish single choices. The research strongly supports dietary flexibility: people who allow occasional indulgences maintain healthier habits long-term than those who follow strict elimination rules. Log honestly, notice patterns, and adjust gradually.
section5.imageCaption: Consistency over weeks matters far more than any single meal

section6.title: Why we support multiple diets
section6.body: Mediterranean, DASH, plant-based, ketogenic, flexitarian — the evidence base behind each of these approaches has merit, and the right choice depends on your health goals, preferences, cultural background, and medical history. Rather than picking one and pushing it, NutriApp lets you select your preferred dietary framework and tailors feedback to it. What all well-researched diets share is an emphasis on whole foods, adequate protein, and limiting ultra-processed products.

section7.title: Intermittent fasting and meal timing
section7.body: Time-restricted eating — eating within a defined daily window — has gained substantial research support for metabolic health, insulin sensitivity, and weight management. The most studied pattern is 16:8: a 16-hour fasting window and an 8-hour eating window. Importantly, intermittent fasting is not a licence to eat poorly within the window; food quality still matters. NutriApp supports IF patterns through its flexible logging — you can track what you eat without being penalised for when you eat.

section8.title: Checking products on your phone
section8.body: The barcode scanner in NutriApp is a phone-first feature. Open the menu on your phone, tap "Check product", and point your camera at the barcode of any packaged food. NutriApp looks it up in a database of over 3 million products and returns an instant breakdown — calories, protein, carbs, fat, fibre, sugar, and sodium — alongside a processing level score.
section8.novaTitle: What the processing level score means
section8.novaBody: The score is based on the NOVA classification system, a research framework developed by nutritional epidemiologists to categorise foods by the degree and purpose of processing. It runs from 1 to 4, shown as coloured squares:
section8.nova1: NOVA 1 — Unprocessed or minimally processed (fresh fruit, plain meat, eggs, plain yoghurt). Four green squares.
section8.nova2: NOVA 2 — Processed culinary ingredients (olive oil, flour, sugar, butter, salt). These are not eaten alone but used to prepare food. Two green squares.
section8.nova3: NOVA 3 — Processed foods (canned vegetables, cheese, cured meat, freshly baked bread). Three amber squares.
section8.nova4: NOVA 4 — Ultra-processed (soft drinks, packaged snacks, instant noodles, reconstituted meat products). Four red squares.
section8.novaConclusion: A NOVA 4 result is not a ban — it is information. Use it alongside the nutritional breakdown to decide whether a product fits your goals and how often you want it in your diet.

closing.title: The bottom line
closing.body: Eat mostly whole foods. Include plenty of protein and fibre. Limit ultra-processed products. Find a pattern you can sustain. Log what you eat — not to obsess, but to understand. That is the philosophy behind every feature in NutriApp.
